title: Controller skills — assess_drift, nudge, render_verdict (Epic 4, issue #35)
prompt:
Implement controller skills: assess_drift(message, side) -> {captured, reason, confidence}; nudge(agent, reason) -> private correction; render_verdict(transcript) -> structured verdict. See docs/prds/anti-sycophancy.md.

Follow repo standards: TDD (write the failing test first, then code); max 150 lines per code file (split, don't compress); ruff = 0 violations + mypy clean; no hard-coded values (read from config); every external API call goes through the API gatekeeper (Epic 13); log via the LOG package; keep coverage >= 85%. Read docs/PRD.md and the relevant docs/prds/*.md before starting.

usage.summary: usage to be filled by main loop from harness report

note: Third batch of Epic 4 (PRD §5.2/§5.3, docs/prds/anti-sycophancy.md §2-§4) — the CONTROLLER's three skills, mirroring the pure/deterministic structuring style of build_argument (4.2) and analyze_opponent (4.3). Added skills/controller.py (the three functions, 48 code lines) + five new models in skills/models.py (DriftRequest, DriftAssessment, NudgeMessage, TranscriptTurn, VerdictRequest, Verdict) + concession-phrase list / confidence weights / reason+correction+rationale templates / tie label as named constants in constants.py (no hard-coded values inline). Re-exported from agent_debate.core.skills and agent_debate.core. PURE/NO-NETWORK skills: the controller LLM supplies judgement as arguments; the skills validate + arrange it, making NO LLM/network call, so the API gatekeeper (Epic 13) is N/A here (noted per task). (1) assess_drift(message, side, signals?) -> DriftAssessment {captured: bool, reason: str, confidence: float in [0,1]}: caller-supplied signals (controller-LLM heuristics) force captured (conf 0.9); else a deterministic concession-phrase scan over the text (DRIFT_CONCESSION_PHRASES, conf 0.6) flags 'you're right'/'i agree'/'i concede'/etc; else not captured (conf 0.1). Side validated via a TypeAdapter(DebateSide) (bad side -> ValidationError, not bare ValueError); message non-emptiness via DriftRequest. Epic 8.1 deepens the detector from these one-source constants. (2) nudge(agent, reason) -> NudgeMessage {target, reason, correction, is_debate_turn=False}: a private correction that re-anchors the side and is logged as a 'nudge' LogEvent but per anti-sycophancy §2.4/§4 does NOT count as a debate turn (is_debate_turn always False). (3) render_verdict(transcript | VerdictRequest) -> Verdict {winner: side|'tie', rationale, scores: per-side totals}: winner is DERIVED from the transcript — either the controller-LLM-supplied winner/rationale (VerdictRequest) used verbatim, or a per-side score tally (tie when equal); the Verdict exposes ONLY debate-derived fields (winner/rationale/scores) and NEVER a pre-held controller stance (PRD §5.3 'controller never reveals its own stance' — asserted by a test that the dumped keys are exactly {winner, rationale, scores}). Logs verdict via a 'verdict' LogEvent. TDD red-first: wrote packages/core/tests/test_controller_skills.py (20 tests), watched it fail (ImportError: cannot import name 'DriftAssessment'), implemented to green. Gates green locally: uv sync clean; ruff check . = All checks passed; ruff format --check . clean (89 files); mypy = no issues in 89 source files; pytest --cov = 336 passed, 100% coverage on controller.py + models.py, 99.81% total (>=85 required); check_line_limit.py rc=0; secret_scan.py rc=0. NOT over-built: full assess_drift detector (Epic 8.1) and verdict scoring (Epic 8.3) and Pydantic AI tool registration (4.5) are deferred.
